text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Economics Minister Guntars Krasts refused to confirm the candidatures of two directors of the privatization agency. The minister believes the two directors should be replaced by his party members, Andris Grinbergs, former executive director of Riga city council and Anrijs Brencans, who chaired the city's development commission.
- The privatization agency has approved the basic rules for privatisation of Ventspils Nafta and LaSam.
- The cabinet approved the draft law on border guards, which states that the service is controlled by the interior ministry.
- The foreign ministry has received a note from the Russian embassy saying the Soviet-era Victory monument in Riga has been damaged and needs to be repaired.
- 17 deputies did not submit their income declarations in good time.
- The ozone layer above Latvia has become again much thinner in recent days.
DIENA
- The Bank of Latvia announced the decision to have its rate of discount reduced to five percent a year.
- EU Commissioner Hans Van den Broek will be visiting Latvia on April 3-4. He will formally open a new EU office in Riga.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- Polish ambassador Jaroslaw Bartkiewicz met Prime Minister Andris Shkele to discuss relations between the two countries.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- On April 2 the two strategic investors of Latvian Gas are due to sign agreement with the privatisation agency on buying 32.5 percent of the company's stock.
- Transportation Minister Vilis Krishtopans said Latvian roads need a minimum yearly investment of $70-100 million to be kept in order.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The shares of the Riga railway coach-building plant will be sold for privatisation vouchers. The privatisation agency believes it to have a good perspective.
- SAS Radisson hotel is to host the Baltic drink fair on April 23-25.
